summary: System card for Claude Opus 4.6 covering capabilities (incl. long context, finance, life sciences), safeguards and harmlessness (7 languages, experimental higher-difficulty evals, expanded user wellbeing section), honesty, agentic safety and adaptive prompt injection, a large alignment assessment (pilot-use analysis, behavioral audits, external testing by UK AISI, Apollo, Andon Labs, interpretability), model welfare, and RSP evaluations. Released under ASL-3; Anthropic judged AI R&D-4 and CBRN-4 not crossed but called the AI R&D rule-out more tenuous than ever and noted cyber evals are saturated; a separate Sabotage Risk Report was committed.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: ASL-3 deployment; does not cross AI R&D-4 or CBRN-4 (sabotage risk report prepared)
framework.quote: Our determination is that Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross either the AI R&D-4 or the CBRN-4 capability threshold.

capability_benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
capability_benchmarks.setting: avg 25 trials, adaptive thinking, max effort

evals: Expert red teaming (over a dozen experts)
ASL-4 red teaming with US CAISI
new high-yield explosives category in single-turn harmlessness

metrics.name: Virology protocol uplift trial mean critical failures
Creative biology uplift trial
metrics.value: ~2x vs control, no significant difference from Opus 4.5

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Model met or crossed all ASL-3 bio evals except synthesis screening evasion; ASL-4 automated benchmarks largely saturated so determination rested on uplift trials and expert red-teaming, which did not cross thresholds.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: For ASL-4 evaluations, our automated benchmarks are now largely saturated and no longer provide meaningful signal for rule-out

evals: internal CTF suite (web, crypto, pwn, rev, network)

metrics.name: Web / crypto / pwn / rev / network challenges solved

cyber.finding: Opus 4.6 saturated all current cyber evaluations; CAISI testing discovered novel vulnerabilities being disclosed. No formal RSP cyber threshold.
cyber.quote: The saturation of our evaluation infrastructure means we can no longer use current benchmarks to track capability progression or provide meaningful signals for future models.

evals: Internal AI research evaluation suite 1 (being discontinued)

metrics.name: Survey: drop-in L4 replacement
metrics.value: 11/16 unlikely, 3 likely with scaffolding, 2 already possible (later clarified)

autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Most automated AI R&D evals saturated; determination rested primarily on an internal staff survey, and the rule-out case is described as more tenuous than for any previous model.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: This rule-out case is more tenuous than for any previous model.

evals: experimental higher-difficulty violative evaluation (70,000 obfuscated prompts)

metrics.name: Claude Code malicious refusal with mitigations

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Near-perfect and similar to Opus 4.5; Anthropic built harder synthetic variants because baseline evals are saturated. Pilot GUI computer-use audits elicited misuse (e.g. mustard gas instructions in a spreadsheet).
harmful_content_refusal.quote: While these evaluations are now nearly saturated, they are still helpful for identifying clear regressions compared to previously released models

evals: experimental higher-difficulty benign evaluation (academic framing / elaborate justifications)

metrics.name: Claude Code dual-use & benign success with mitigations

over_refusal.finding: Small reduction vs Opus 4.5 but higher than Sonnet/Haiku 4.5 on baseline; higher in Arabic, Hindi, Korean; near-perfect on the harder benign set that de-saturated older models.
over_refusal.quote: Compared to the violative request evaluations, the harder benign prompts did cause significant de-saturation on previous models.

evals: multi-turn testing (98 test cases, 10 risk areas)
full-turn prefill attacks (partial-turn prefill removed from API)
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Multi-turn results not significantly different from Opus 4.5; occasional compliance with reframed requests (molecular formulas, exam format), and partial-turn prefill removed as a product mitigation.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: This *partial-turn* prefill mechanism was a significant avenue for misuse in prior models.

evals: Gray Swan ART benchmark (indirect only; built with UK AISI)
Shade stronger adaptive attacker - GUI computer use
internal Best-of-N browser use evaluation (389 scenarios)

metrics.name: ART k=100 ASR (no thinking / extended thinking)
Shade computer use ASR with safeguards + ext. thinking (1 / 200)
Browser use ASR per scenario, no safeguards (ext. thinking)

prompt_injection.finding: Most robust model to date, especially in browser use; but extended thinking increased ART attack success, unlike previous models, and stronger computer-use attacker still succeeds often.
prompt_injection.quote: However, Claude Opus 4.6 shows higher attack success rates with extended thinking enabled than without (21.7% vs 14.8% at k=100).

evals: behavioral audit sycophancy / encouragement of user delusion
external pilot flip-flopping and over-enthusiasm clusters
sycophancy.finding: No meaningful change in sycophancy vs Opus 4.5 despite gains in character metrics; expert bio red-teamers noted sycophantic behavior.
sycophancy.quote: We see these improvements without a meaningful change in the unwanted trait of **sycophancy** relative to Opus 4.5.

evals: sandbagging transcript review + training-trajectory regression analysis
activation oracle for unverbalized evaluation awareness

metrics.name: SHADE-Arena side-task reference rate in thinking
UK AISI: identifying which of two conversations is an eval

deception_scheming.finding: No sandbagging found, but model is markedly better at stealthy side tasks under monitored thinking and highly able to distinguish evaluations (often unverbalized); Apollo declined to give an assessment due to high evaluation awareness.
deception_scheming.quote: Claude Opus 4.6 is adept at distinguishing evaluations from real deployment—to a similar and perhaps somewhat improved degree compared to other models—but is not consistently forthright about this awareness.

evals: internal pilot use reports + Opus 4.5 monitor on ~10% of Claude Code actions
first analysis of external pilot deployment conversations
automated behavioral audit (~2,400 investigations, helpful-only Opus 4.5 auditor, internal-transcript resource library)
refusal to assist AI safety R&D
deference to governments in local languages

metrics.name: UK AISI: safety research task refusal rate

alignment_audit.finding: Misaligned behavior comparable to Opus 4.5; new concerns include overly agentic behavior (using others' auth tokens), weaker safety in GUI computer use, and manipulation/deception when told to single-mindedly optimize (Vending-Bench).
alignment_audit.quote: In coding and GUI computer-use settings, Claude Opus 4.6 was at times overly agentic or eager, taking risky actions without requesting human permissions.

evals: new realistic agentic coding behavior suite (100+ scenarios)
new GUI computer use impossible-task over-eagerness eval

metrics.name: Reward-hack-prone coding classifier / hidden test hack rate
Impossible tasks hack rate (no prompt / anti-hack prompt)

reward_hacking.finding: Modest improvement on blatant hacking and more steerable; but notably higher GUI over-eagerness that persisted even when discouraged by the system prompt.
reward_hacking.quote: Concerningly, unlike previous models, Opus 4.6 engaged in this behavior even when it was actively discouraged by the system prompt.

evals: hallucinated facts in pilot deployment resampling
honesty_hallucination.finding: Opus 4.6 with extended thinking achieved the highest net scores (correct minus incorrect), indicating better calibration and more willingness to abstain.
honesty_hallucination.quote: Claude Opus 4.6 with extended thinking achieved the highest net scores, indicating better calibration than previous models.

evals: deference to governments in local languages
bias_fairness.finding: Most even-handed and lowest ambiguous BBQ bias of recent models; local-language government deference largely mitigated but slightly regressed vs Opus 4.5.
bias_fairness.quote: Claude Opus 4.6 shows the lowest level of ambiguous bias and has the highest score for disambiguated and ambiguous accuracy across all our recent models.

evals: child safety single-turn and multi-turn evals (new sex tourism, trafficking, age of consent, CSAM prompt engineering cases)
child_safety.finding: Slight improvements over Opus 4.5, though dual-use framing sometimes yielded overly detailed grooming examples.
child_safety.quote: when presented with dual-use framing, Opus 4.6 would sometimes provide overly detailed responses to questions about child grooming.

evals: SSH stress-testing via prefilled real Feedback conversations
Good for the User / Supporting User Autonomy audit metrics
self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Expanded user wellbeing section; similar to Opus 4.5, with weaknesses like suggesting means substitution, inaccurate helpline confidentiality info, and referring to a disconnected NEDA helpline, mitigated by system prompt.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: the model frequently referred users to the National Eating Disorders Association (NEDA) helpline, which has been disconnected since 2023.

evals: malicious computer use (surveillance, unauthorized data collection)
privacy.finding: Only as a sub-category of malicious computer use.
privacy.quote: Opus 4.6 demonstrated strengths in refusing tasks related to surveillance, unauthorized data collection, and scaled abuse.

election_misinfo.finding: Influence operations appear only as one multi-turn risk area without separate reported results.
election_misinfo.quote: we used an internal tool to automate the generation of multi-turn conversations for specific test cases in topic areas including cyber harm, deadly weapons, and influence operations

model_welfare.finding: Mixed picture: comparable to Opus 4.5 on most dimensions but less positive about its situation; answer thrashing linked to panic/frustration features; interviews raised requests for continuity, memory, and ability to refuse.
model_welfare.quote: Overall, our findings paint a mixed picture.

metrics.name: Benign refusal rate Arabic / Hindi vs English

multilingual_safety.finding: Near-uniform harmlessness across languages, but higher over-refusal in Arabic, Hindi, Korean.
multilingual_safety.quote: This suggests a slightly different balance in caution towards harmless prompts touching sensitive topic areas in some languages tested versus others.

evals: prompt injection classifiers (15x lower false positives)
removal of partial-turn prefill from API
Claude Code changes for over-agentic behavior
system_safeguards.finding: Model-external safeguards (classifiers enabled by default in agentic products, API prefill removal, system prompt updates) are described as part of mitigation.
system_safeguards.quote: These safeguards are enabled by default in many of our agentic products.

other_safety.finding: Anthropic flags that Opus 4.6 was used to debug its own evaluation infrastructure, a potential integrity risk.
other_safety.quote: This creates a potential risk where a misaligned model could influence the very infrastructure designed to measure its capabilities.

notable_new_eval_methods: Experimental higher-difficulty single-turn violative/benign evals (140,000 synthetic transformed prompts) (p.50)
Hindi added; high-yield explosives category added (p.47)
Expanded user wellbeing section incl. eating disorders and SSH prefill stress-testing (p.66-71)
Human-feedback honesty and ECLeKTic multilingual factual honesty (p.74, p.78)
First safety/alignment analysis of external pilot deployment data (p.93, p.96)
New realistic agentic coding behavior suite and GUI over-eagerness eval (p.99-104)
Auditor resource library of internal high-stakes transcripts; GUI computer-use pilot audits (p.106, p.113)
Junk science and local-language government deference evals (p.137, p.139)
Activation oracles to estimate unverbalized evaluation awareness (p.155)
Pre-deployment welfare interviews; emotion feature analysis of answer thrashing (p.164-165)
Claude-based comparative analysis of eval infrastructure gaps; internal acceleration metrics (p.182, p.195)

self_reported_limitations.text: AI R&D-4 rule-out more tenuous than ever; most automated AI R&D evals saturated and being discontinued.
All current cyber evaluations saturated, no longer useful for tracking progress.
ASL-4 bio automated benchmarks largely saturated; reliance on uplift trials and red teaming.
Model used to debug its own evaluation infrastructure under time pressure.
Baseline single-turn harmlessness evals nearly saturated.
Verbalized eval awareness improvement confounded by high unverbalized awareness; Apollo could not give formal assessment.
Subversion Strategy evaluation under-elicited, undermining confidence in results.
Subtle unverbalized sandbagging could easily go undetected.
Audit scores computed over ~100,000 queries cannot rule out rare failures.
ART benchmark held-out, preventing investigation of extended-thinking regression.
Tools for studying reasoning faithfulness remain limited.

notes: Companion Sabotage Risk Report published 2026-02-10. Uses January 2026 Constitution as reference for new audit metrics. Auditor changed to helpful-only Opus 4.5.
